title: Evidence priority mapper and SIEM handshake guide
content:
Purpose and context:
This note defines a lightweight, practical design for mapping collected audit/evidence events to an internal priority score (0..100), and the minimal handshake payload we push to downstream SIEMs and forensic stores. The goal is to enable fast triage, reliable retention decisions, and predictable SIEM ingestion without overloading customers or the export pipeline.

Scope:
- Applies to control evidence generated by RBAC v2 changes, policy evaluations, privileged operations, and collector-side telemetry used for compliance and forensics.
- Not covering telemetry traces, metrics-only telemetry, or non-audit logs.
- Intended for Redwood-hosted evidence synchronization and for customers that subscribe to SIEM exports via S3/forwarder or direct syslog endpoints.

High-level principles:
1) Deterministic minimalism: the exported record must contain a small canonical set of fields that any SIEM can parse and act on. Keep payload <= 6KB.
2) Priority-first routing: every event gets an evidence_priority (0..100) computed using deterministic rule weights. Consumers use thresholds to route to realtime alerting, cold archive, or legal hold.
3) RBAC-aware enrichment: when the event is tied to an RBAC v2 delta or evaluation, include normalized role/actor/namespace buckets (no raw policy text).
4) Privacy-preserving: PII must be pseudonymized prior to export (see masking rules).
5) Backwards compatibility: new fields are additive and use clearly versioned envelope: schema_version.

Envelope definition (plain fields to include in exported record):
- schema_version: string (e.g. v1.2)
- event_id: string (uuid v4)
- event_ts: string (RFC3339)
- source: string (collector/route id)
- evidence_type: string (rbac_change | policy_eval | privileged_op | config_export)
- actor_id_hash: string (sha256 hex of actor id + tenant salt)
- actor_role_bucket: string (owner|admin|app-service|readonly|external)
- target_resource: string (resource path, normalized)
- action: string (grant_role|revoke_role|evaluate|exec_sensitive|token_create)
- evidence_priority: string (integer 0-100 as string)
- reason_codes: comma separated short codes (PRIV_OP,RBAC_ESCALATION,FAILED_AUTH,EXPORT_TOOLS)
- retention_tier: string (hot|warm|cold|legal-hold)
- small_message: string (short human summary, 1-2 sentences)
- raw_proof_uri: string (internal object store path or presigned link)
- signature_meta: string (signed-by, sig-ts)
- export_checksum: string (sha256 of canonical payload)

Notes: keep actor identifiers hashed. raw_proof_uri links should be ACL-protected; SIEMs that cannot reach Redwood storage will receive an alternative summary-only payload with raw_proof_uri set to "N/A".

Priority mapping rules (recommended base weights):
The evidence_priority is computed as sum of weighted signals, then clamped to [0,100]. We recommend implementing as integer math on the collector for deterministic export. Example signals and nominal weights: 
- scope_multiplier: system|org|tenant (system=1.2, org=1.0, tenant=0.9)
- actor_role_weight: owner=40, admin=30, app-service=18, external=45, readonly=5
- action_weight: grant_role=25, revoke_role=10, exec_sensitive=35, token_create=20, policy_eval=8
- policy_risk_score: (0..30) derived from policy tags (sensitive, network, billing)
- failure_multiplier: failed authorization or replayed event *1.3
- historical_noise_discount: if same actor+resource has repeated low-risk events in last 24h, subtract up to 12 points

Example calculation (pseudo):
base = actor_role_weight + action_weight + policy_risk_score
base *= scope_multiplier
if failed then base = base * 1.3
base -= historical_noise_discount
evidence_priority = clamp(round(base), 0, 100)

Sample mappings (quick reference):
- Org owner revoking another owner role for org-level resource: owner(40) + revoke_role(10) + policy_risk(10) * 1.0 = 60 -> priority 60
- External agent exec_sensitive on tenant resource: external(45) + exec_sensitive(35) + policy_risk(8) *0.9 -> ~77 -> priority 77
- Readonly token_create: 5 + 20 = 25 -> discount -> priority 25

Retention tier assignment rules (used by downstream archivist):
- If evidence_priority >= 80 -> legal-hold (must be stored immutable, retention > 7 years until released)
- If 50 <= evidence_priority < 80 -> hot (30d, encrypted) + searchable index pushed to SIEM
- If 20 <= evidence_priority < 50 -> warm (180d)
- If evidence_priority < 20 -> cold (30d metadata, event stub)

RBAC v2 enrichment guidance:
- Don’t export raw role policy. Instead include role_hash and role_category tag (privileged, infra, billing, app). role_hash = sha256(role_name+tenant_id)
- For evaluation events include: decision (allow|deny|conditional), policy_tags (comma list), evaluation_id
- Map role membership deltas to action values: grant_role, revoke_role, rotate_credentials

Audit schema example (stringified JSON snippet for implementers):
{"audit": {"schema_version":"v1.2","event_id":"uuid-v4","ts":"2026-03-10T15:22:33Z","type":"rbac_change","actor_hash":"<sha256>","actor_bucket":"admin","resource":"/orgs/acme/projects/alpha","action":"grant_role","role_hash":"<sha256>","role_category":"privileged","policy_tags":"network,critical","outcome":"success","meta":"..."}}

Note: The export above must be transmitted as a single line JSON to SIEM syslog to avoid multiline ingestion issues. Also include the canonical envelope fields listed earlier.

SIEM handshake and export modes:
Mode A: Direct syslog push (recommended for realtime alerting)
- Transport: TLS over TCP, syslog RFC5424 framing.
- Payload: one-line JSON envelope with schema_version and compressed small_message.
- Authentication: mTLS client cert, with cert CN mapped to customer connector id.
- Rate limiting: upstream collectors must honor per-customer qps limits. High priority events bypass soft-limits but must be rate-limited absolute (no more than 10/sec per tenant) to avoid floods.

Mode B: S3 delivery (batch, recommended for long-term ingestion)
- Objects: gzip newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with envelope records.
- Partition keys: /YYYY/MM/DD/tenant_id/priority_bucket/part-xxxxx.gz
- Manifest: once per hour, manifest JSON listing objects + md5s.

Mode C: Forwarder webhook (customer-managed)
- Signed POST with HMAC header, small batch size <= 500 records.

Masking and PII rules (collector-side):
- Email addresses: mask local part keeping domain, e.g., a***@example.com
- User IDs: store hashed id, keep actor_display short string if allowed with opt-in (e.g., user-firstname).
- IPs: keep /24 prefix for external addresses, last octet replaced with 0.

Operational runbooks and workflow for control evidence triage:
1) Collector emits prioritized event -> routed to export queue and internal triage queue if priority >= 70.
2) Triage queue triggers async enrichment jobs that attach related session logs and policy snapshots. Enrichment must complete in <= 5 minutes.
3) If enrichment fails after retries, mark evidence_priority += 5 and add reason_code ENRICH_FAIL.
4) If priority >= 90 after enrichment -> pager duty escalation (security-oncall).
5) All legal-hold assignments trigger a duplicate copy to immutable storage service and notify compliance@redwood.com.

Producer/consumer compatibility and versioning:
- schema_version must be included in every export. Consumers reading unknown schema_version should fallback to basic fields (event_id,event_ts,source,evidence_type,evidence_priority,small_message).
- Additive fields are safe; removed fields require deprecation cycle of 6 months and notice.

Collector implementation notes for serving-runtime team:
- Implement deterministic hashing using tenant salt from KMS (rotate every 6 months).
- Compute evidence_priority locally to avoid reordering issues in transport.
- Use embedded lightweight rule engine (yaml rules + weights) so security can tune mapping without deploy cycle. Example rule yaml: 
  rules:
    - id: external_exec_sensitive
      when: actor_bucket == external && action == exec_sensitive
      add: 80

- Emit metric (collector.evidence.priority.dist) and histogram buckets: 0-19,20-49,50-79,80-100.

Testing and validation checklist:
- Unit tests for priority mapping covering role permutations and scope multipliers.
- End-to-end test that verifies S3 objects contain valid ndjson and manifest matches checksums.
- Chaos test: simulate 10k low-priority events and ensure no hot route flooding.

Open questions and decisions required:
- Should the priority range be 0..100 or 0..1000? (proposal: keep 0..100 for human interpretability)
- Legal-hold: who has authority to remove legal-hold? Proposed: compliance lead + legal advisor.
- Masking policy opt-in for internal debugging: how long to keep unhashed debug actor mapping? (proposal: 7 days)

Action items:
- (Sana) Draft a YAML rule reference and share with SecOps by 2026-03-18.
- (Elliot) Prototype syslog one-line exporter and test with Splunk forwarder by 2026-03-24.
- (Marco) Add unit tests for hashing and priority calculation in collector-lib by 2026-03-20.
- (Priya) Draft compliance note describing legal-hold flow and requestable unlock by 2026-03-22.

Appendix: short glossary:
- evidence_priority: integer 0..100 used for routing and retention decisions.
- raw_proof_uri: internal object store path containing full artifacts (screenshots, logs).
- role_hash: stable hash of role name+tenant used as a pointer (no policy text).

-- end of guide --
